zh.summary: Cyber Kill Chain 看階段，MITRE ATT&CK 看目的與行為；分類不是成功證明，結論要跟著證據走。

sourceBody.text: CEH M01-05｜Cyber Kill Chain、MITRE ATT&CK
Module 01：Introduction to Ethical Hacking（道德駭客入門）
一、先說結論：一個看整段攻擊，一個看具體行為
這堂課先記住兩句話：
Cyber Kill Chain 幫你整理「攻擊大致走到哪個階段」；MITRE ATT&CK® 幫你描述「對方為了什麼目的，做了什麼行為」。
兩者可以一起使用，但不是同一張表換個名字，也不是一格對一格的翻譯。
想像一間咖啡廳正在調查失竊案。你可以用「事前觀察、準備工具、進入店內、拿走財物」整理整件事；也可以更細地描述「冒充送貨員」「使用失竊鑰匙」「打開收銀機」。前者比較像階段地圖，後者比較像行為分類。
資安事件也是如此。只說「被駭了」太模糊，直接堆一串工具名稱也不夠。我們需要把目的、行為、證據與防護連起來。
這兩套框架適合用來閱讀事件報告、整理已取得的紀錄、檢查偵測缺口，以及設計經授權的驗證。前提是先知道評估範圍、系統環境與證據來源；框架本身不會授予你測試別人的權限。本課只有紙上案例，不操作任何真實目標。
二、Cyber Kill Chain：先把七個階段分清楚

Cyber Kill Chain 常譯為「網路攻擊鏈」，由 Lockheed Martin 提出。本課採用原本的七階段模型，不把其他延伸版本混進來。它的防禦重點不是等攻擊全部走完，而是找出可以發現或阻斷的環節。[Lockheed Martin：Cyber Kill Chain](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/capabilities/cyber/cyber-kill-chain.html)
1. Reconnaissance（偵察）

items: 白話意思：蒐集目標資訊，了解可能的接觸點。

sourceBody.text: 2. Weaponization（武器化）

items: 白話意思：把利用方式與惡意程式等準備成可投遞內容。

sourceBody.text: 3. Delivery（投遞）

items: 白話意思：把惡意內容送到目標環境。

sourceBody.text: 4. Exploitation（利用）

items: 白話意思：觸發弱點或其他執行條件，讓攻擊程式碼運作。

sourceBody.text: 5. Installation（安裝）

items: 白話意思：在環境中安裝惡意元件，建立立足點。

sourceBody.text: 6. Command and Control，C2（命令與控制）

items: 白話意思：建立供攻擊者下指令、取得回應的通訊。

sourceBody.text: 7. Actions on Objectives（達成攻擊目的的行動）

items: 白話意思：進行竊取、竄改、破壞或中斷服務等目標行動。

sourceBody.text: 七階段的名稱與基本意義可對照原始模型及 EC-Council 的說明。[Lockheed Martin 原始論文](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/content/dam/lockheed-martin/rms/documents/cyber/LM-White-Paper-Intel-Driven-Defense.pdf)、[EC-Council：七階段介紹](https://www.eccouncil.org/cybersecurity-exchange/incident-handling/cyber-kill-chain-seven-steps-cyberattack/)
初學者最容易把中間幾步混在一起，這裡拆清楚：

items: 收到惡意附件，不等於附件已執行。「送到了」與「真的觸發了」是兩件事。
程式碼執行，不等於已安裝持續存取機制。一次執行與之後能否再次進入，要分別查證。
存在 C2，不等於已取得所有權限或已偷走資料。能下指令、指令成功執行、資料成功外傳，仍是不同結論。

sourceBody.text: 這張地圖也不是要求每一種攻擊都得出現七個完整、可見的步驟。例如，單純濫用已取得的雲端帳號，不一定需要先在受害電腦安裝惡意程式。事件證據不符合某一步，就保留不適用或未知，不要為了讓故事完整而硬補。
三、MITRE ATT&CK：把「為什麼」和「怎麼做」分開
ATT&CK 的全名是 Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge。你可以把它理解成一套持續維護的攻擊者行為知識庫，內容以實際觀察到的行為為基礎，不是掃描工具，也不是一份保證涵蓋所有攻擊的清單。[MITRE ATT&CK 入門](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/)
先分清四個層次：
Tactic（戰術）

items: 要回答的問題：這一步想達到什麼目的？
白話例子：Initial Access：想取得最初的存取機會。

sourceBody.text: Technique（技術）

items: 要回答的問題：用哪一類方法達到目的？
白話例子：Phishing：透過釣魚方式接觸並誘導目標。

sourceBody.text: Sub-technique（子技術）

items: 要回答的問題：這一類方法中，更具體的是哪一種？
白話例子：Spearphishing Attachment：用針對性的惡意郵件附件。

sourceBody.text: Procedure（具體做法）

items: 要回答的問題：在某個事件中，實際怎麼使用這種方法？
白話例子：某封假冒供應商的郵件，把惡意檔案包裝成採購明細。

sourceBody.text: 戰術是目的；技術是方法；子技術是更細的方法分類；具體做法是事件中的實際實現。最後一列是本課的假想示例，不是 MITRE 收錄的真實事件。[MITRE：四種術語的定義](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/faq/)
以這組真實存在的編號為例：
Initial Access → Phishing（T1566）→ Spearphishing Attachment（T1566.001）
T1566.001 是行為分類編號，不是漏洞編號，也不是「攻擊成功」的認證。MITRE 把這個子技術放在 Initial Access 戰術下，但名稱表示行為的目的與類型；一封被攔截的釣魚附件，仍可能呈現這種嘗試，不代表對方成功進來。[MITRE：T1566.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/)
你之後還會看到 Execution（執行）、Persistence（持續存取）、Discovery（環境探索）、Lateral Movement（橫向移動）、Collection（蒐集資料）、Exfiltration（資料外傳）等戰術。現在不用背完全部編號；先學會看到一個行為時，問「它想做到什麼？證據顯示怎麼做？」就好。
四、兩套框架怎麼一起用？不要當成固定闖關表
主要視角

items: Cyber Kill Chain：攻擊活動的階段
MITRE ATT&CK：攻擊者行為與目的

sourceBody.text: 適合回答

items: Cyber Kill Chain：這段活動進展到哪裡？哪裡能中斷？
MITRE ATT&CK：具體用了什麼方法？我們能否偵測？

sourceBody.text: 呈現方式

items: Cyber Kill Chain：七階段的概念鏈
MITRE ATT&CK：戰術、技術及子技術的分類

sourceBody.text: 常見誤用

items: Cyber Kill Chain：沒證據也把七步填滿
MITRE ATT&CK：把矩陣從左到右當成必走流程

sourceBody.text: ATT&CK 不是時間表。攻擊者可能重複某個行為、跳過某些戰術，或同時進行不同活動；矩陣中相鄰的欄位，不代表時間上一定先後發生。[CISA：ATT&CK Mapping 最佳實務](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/publications/Best%20Practices%20for%20MITRE%20ATTCK%20Mapping.pdf)
兩者也沒有一對一關係。Cyber Kill Chain 的「Actions on Objectives」範圍很大；在更細的行為分析中，可能涉及資料蒐集、資料外傳或破壞等不同目的。因此，不能看到第七階段，就自動填入所有相關 ATT&CK 技術。
另外，ATT&CK 描述的是行為。即使兩起事件都用了同一種釣魚方法，也不能單憑同一個編號，認定背後是同一個人或組織。
五、具體例子：Northstar 收到一封「採購明細」郵件
以下完全是假想教學情境。Northstar 是線上教材平台，員工電腦可處理一般工作，但沒有讀取學生私人作答資料的權限。
假設調查人員在合法授權下，取得了郵件、終端與存取紀錄，形成以下案例：
郵件冒充供應商；不清楚對方如何知道聯絡人。

items: 可支持的判讀：偵察來源仍未知。
證據界線：不能直接斷定公司通訊錄被竊取。

sourceBody.text: 附件分析確認它包含惡意內容。

items: 可支持的判讀：可分析武器化後的成品。
證據界線：不代表知道在哪裡、何時、由誰製作。

sourceBody.text: 郵件紀錄確認該附件送達員工信箱。

items: 可支持的判讀：Delivery；其針對性惡意附件行為可對照 T1566.001。
證據界線：送達不等於開啟或執行。

sourceBody.text: 另有終端與樣本證據，確認閱讀程式的弱點被利用而執行惡意程式碼。

items: 可支持的判讀：Exploitation；可對照 T1203。
證據界線：不是所有「開啟附件」都符合這個結論。

sourceBody.text: 終端紀錄確認惡意元件被寫入並安裝。

items: 可支持的判讀：Installation。
證據界線：仍不能只靠寫入檔案，就說重新開機後一定能持續存取。

sourceBody.text: 關聯分析確認該元件透過 HTTPS 交換攻擊指令與回應。

items: 可支持的判讀：C2；可對照 T1071.001。
證據界線：不是看到 HTTPS 連線就能判為 C2。

sourceBody.text: 惡意程序嘗試讀取學生私人資料，但被存取控制拒絕。

items: 可支持的判讀：有朝攻擊目的前進的嘗試；這次讀取被阻擋。
證據界線：不能宣稱資料已外洩，也不能因此保證所有資料都安全。

sourceBody.text: 這裡的 T1203 是「利用用戶端軟體漏洞來執行程式碼」；只有相應證據存在時才套用，不把所有附件執行都塞進去。[MITRE：T1203](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/)
T1071.001 則描述利用 Web 協定進行 C2 的行為。HTTPS 同時也大量用於正常工作，所以需要程序、目的地、時間與通訊用途等脈絡；協定名稱本身不能證明惡意。[MITRE：T1071.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/)
這個例子真正要練的，不是「貼了幾個標籤」，而是：每個標籤旁邊，都有能支持它的觀察，以及不能超過的結論界線。
六、防護要回到「擋什麼、看什麼、怎麼驗證」
沿用上面的假想案例，我們可以提出以下防護設計；是否有效，仍要在自己的授權環境中驗證，不能光看產品已安裝。
郵件過濾與附件檢查

items: 防護目標：降低惡意內容送到使用者的機會。
驗證重點：郵件到底被阻擋、隔離，還是只有產生警告？

sourceBody.text: 軟體安全更新與執行限制

items: 防護目標：降低弱點被利用及不當程式碼執行的機會。
驗證重點：更新是否實際生效？安全的授權驗證是否符合預期？

sourceBody.text: 終端行為監控

items: 防護目標：發現異常執行、安裝及後續活動。
驗證重點：有沒有對應到正確的裝置、程序與時間？告警是否有人處理？

sourceBody.text: 必要的對外連線限制

items: 防護目標：限制不必要的通訊。
驗證重點：規則是否真的阻擋該連線？正常業務是否仍可使用？

sourceBody.text: 最小權限與資料存取稽核

items: 防護目標：即使某個帳號或程序受影響，也限制可接觸的資料。
驗證重點：用合成資料與授權測試帳號確認：不該讀的被拒絕，該讀的仍能讀。

sourceBody.text: 把防護配置到不同階段，是為了不要只靠單一關卡；AWS 的官方分析也用攻擊鏈整理各階段可採取的偵測與阻斷措施。[AWS：各階段的防禦介入](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/classic-intrusion-analysis-frameworks-for-aws-environments/stopping-intrusion-methods.html)
寫事件結論時，請保持三個習慣：
1. 先寫觀察，再寫分類。例如先寫「郵件紀錄顯示附件被隔離」，不要先寫「入侵成功」再找理由。
2. 區分嘗試、成功與影響。嘗試讀取、讀取成功、複製成功、外傳成功，不是同一件事。
3. 保留未知。沒有紀錄可能是沒發生，也可能是未記錄、保存期限已過或查詢範圍不完整；不能直接把「沒找到」改成「保證沒有」。
同樣地，偵測規則標上 ATT&CK 編號，只代表宣稱要涵蓋某種行為；還要測試資料是否收得到、規則是否有效、誤報是否可接受，以及真的告警時能不能處理。分類不是驗證的替代品。
七、本堂重點與一題小檢核
今天先帶走四件事：

items: Cyber Kill Chain：看階段，找介入點。
MITRE ATT&CK：看目的與行為，讓分析有共同語言。
不硬湊七階段，也不把 ATT&CK 當固定時間順序。
有行為標籤，不等於攻擊成功；結論要跟著證據走。

sourceBody.text: 小檢核：
一家公司收到一封針對性的惡意附件郵件，但郵件閘道已將它隔離。目前沒有找到附件在員工電腦上執行的證據。分析員寫下：「這符合 T1566.001，所以已確認攻擊者成功入侵並竊取資料。」
你會怎麼修正這句結論？用自己的話說一小段就好，不必背編號。
你可以先答這一題；等你實際回答後，我再確認理解。

sourceBody.summary: 展開小檢核參考解答｜白話說明
paragraphs: 比較準確的說法是：「已觀察到針對性的惡意附件郵件投遞嘗試，行為可對照 Spearphishing Attachment（T1566.001）；這封郵件已被閘道隔離，目前沒有足夠證據確認附件在終端執行、攻擊者取得存取權，或資料遭到竊取。」
關鍵在於：T1566.001 是行為分類，不是入侵成功的證明。在 Cyber Kill Chain 的觀點，可以討論投遞環節被攔截；不能因此往後推定利用、安裝、C2 或資料外傳全部發生。
「沒有找到執行證據」也不等於已證明整個環境沒有其他入侵。仍要確認日誌是否完整、是否存在其他郵件副本或攻擊路徑，並把結論限定在已查核的範圍。
展開本解答只供自行核對；沒有收到你的實際回答前，不把本課標成理解通過。

en.summary: Cyber Kill Chain describes stages; MITRE ATT&CK describes objectives and behaviors. Classification is not proof of success.

sourceBody.text: CEH M01-05 | Cyber Kill Chain and MITRE ATT&CK
Module 01: Introduction to Ethical Hacking
1. Conclusion first: one views the overall attack, the other examines specific behaviors
Start by remembering these two ideas:
Cyber Kill Chain helps organize “which broad stage an attack has reached”; MITRE ATT&CK® helps describe “what the adversary did and what they were trying to achieve.”
They can be used together, but they are not the same table under different names, nor a cell-by-cell translation of each other.

Imagine a café investigating a theft. You could organize the overall event as “prior observation, preparing tools, entering the premises and taking property.” You could also describe it more specifically as “impersonating a delivery driver,” “using a stolen key” and “opening the cash register.” The first view resembles a map of stages; the second resembles a classification of behaviors.
Security incidents are similar. Saying only “we were hacked” is too vague, and listing tool names is not enough either. We need to connect objectives, behaviors, evidence and defenses.

These frameworks are useful for reading incident reports, organizing collected records, checking detection gaps and designing authorized validation. First establish the assessment scope, system environment and evidence sources; the frameworks themselves do not authorize you to test someone else's systems. This lesson uses only a tabletop example and operates on no real target.
2. Cyber Kill Chain: distinguish the seven stages first

Cyber Kill Chain was introduced by Lockheed Martin. This lesson uses the original seven-stage model without mixing in other extensions. Its defensive emphasis is not on waiting for an attack to finish, but on identifying places where it can be detected or interrupted. [Lockheed Martin: Cyber Kill Chain](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/en-us/capabilities/cyber/cyber-kill-chain.html)
1. Reconnaissance

items: Plain meaning: gather information about the target and identify possible points of contact.

sourceBody.text: 2. Weaponization

items: Plain meaning: prepare an exploitation mechanism and malicious software or similar components as content that can be delivered.

sourceBody.text: 3. Delivery

items: Plain meaning: send the malicious content into the target environment.

sourceBody.text: 4. Exploitation

items: Plain meaning: trigger a weakness or other execution condition so that attack code runs.

sourceBody.text: 5. Installation

items: Plain meaning: install malicious components in the environment to establish a foothold.

sourceBody.text: 6. Command and Control (C2)

items: Plain meaning: establish communications through which the attacker can issue instructions and receive responses.

sourceBody.text: 7. Actions on Objectives

items: Plain meaning: carry out objective-driven actions such as theft, modification, destruction or service disruption.

sourceBody.text: The seven names and their basic meanings can be compared with the original model and EC-Council's explanation. [Lockheed Martin's original paper](https://www.lockheedmartin.com/content/dam/lockheed-martin/rms/documents/cyber/LM-White-Paper-Intel-Driven-Defense.pdf), [EC-Council: the seven stages](https://www.eccouncil.org/cybersecurity-exchange/incident-handling/cyber-kill-chain-seven-steps-cyberattack/)
Beginners often blur the middle steps together. Separate them carefully:

items: Receiving a malicious attachment does not mean the attachment executed. “It arrived” and “it was actually triggered” are different events.
Code execution does not mean a persistent-access mechanism has been installed. One execution and the ability to return later require separate verification.

The presence of C2 does not mean the attacker has every privilege or has stolen data. Being able to send instructions, successfully executing them and successfully exfiltrating data are different conclusions.

sourceBody.text: This map does not require every attack to exhibit seven complete, visible steps. For example, simply abusing an acquired cloud account does not necessarily require installing malware on a victim's computer. When the incident evidence does not fit a stage, leave it as not applicable or unknown; do not invent steps to complete the story.
3. MITRE ATT&CK: separate “why” from “how”

ATT&CK stands for Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge. Think of it as a continuously maintained knowledge base of adversary behaviors, based on observations from the real world. It is not a scanning tool or a checklist guaranteed to cover every attack. [Getting started with MITRE ATT&CK](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/)
First distinguish four levels:
Tactic

items: Question answered: what objective is this step intended to achieve?
Plain-language example: Initial Access—trying to obtain the first opportunity for access.

sourceBody.text: Technique

items: Question answered: what class of method is used to achieve the objective?
Plain-language example: Phishing—contacting and manipulating a target through phishing.

sourceBody.text: Sub-technique

items: Question answered: which more specific form of that method is used?
Plain-language example: Spearphishing Attachment—using a targeted malicious email attachment.

sourceBody.text: Procedure

items: Question answered: how was the method actually used in a particular incident?
Plain-language example: an email impersonating a supplier disguises a malicious file as a purchase breakdown.

sourceBody.text: A tactic is an objective; a technique is a method; a sub-technique is a more specific category of method; a procedure is its concrete implementation in an incident. The final example is hypothetical teaching material, not a real incident documented by MITRE. [MITRE: definitions of the four terms](https://attack.mitre.org/resources/faq/)
Consider these real identifiers:
Initial Access → Phishing (T1566) → Spearphishing Attachment (T1566.001)

T1566.001 is a behavior classification identifier, not a vulnerability identifier or a certificate of “successful attack.” MITRE places this sub-technique under the Initial Access tactic, but the label describes a behavior's objective and type. A blocked phishing attachment may still represent such an attempt; it does not establish that the adversary got in. [MITRE: T1566.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/)

Later, you will also encounter tactics such as Execution, Persistence, Discovery, Lateral Movement, Collection and Exfiltration. You do not need to memorize every identifier now. First learn to ask, when observing a behavior: “what is it trying to achieve, and what does the evidence show about how it was done?”
4. How can the frameworks be used together? Do not treat them as a fixed progression through levels
Primary perspective

items: Cyber Kill Chain: stages of attack activity.
MITRE ATT&CK: adversary behaviors and objectives.

sourceBody.text: Questions they help answer

items: Cyber Kill Chain: how far has this activity progressed, and where can it be interrupted?
MITRE ATT&CK: which specific methods were used, and can we detect them?

sourceBody.text: Representation

items: Cyber Kill Chain: a conceptual chain of seven stages.
MITRE ATT&CK: a classification of tactics, techniques and sub-techniques.

sourceBody.text: Common misuse

items: Cyber Kill Chain: filling in all seven steps without evidence.
MITRE ATT&CK: treating the matrix from left to right as a mandatory sequence.

sourceBody.text: ATT&CK is not a timeline. Attackers may repeat a behavior, skip tactics or conduct different activities concurrently. Adjacent matrix columns do not imply a necessary chronological order. [CISA: ATT&CK Mapping Best Practices](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/publications/Best%20Practices%20for%20MITRE%20ATTCK%20Mapping.pdf)

There is no one-to-one relationship between the two frameworks either. Cyber Kill Chain's “Actions on Objectives” is broad. More detailed behavioral analysis might involve different objectives such as collection, exfiltration or destruction. Therefore, identifying the seventh stage does not automatically justify adding every related ATT&CK technique.
ATT&CK also describes behavior. Even if two incidents use the same phishing method, a shared identifier alone cannot establish that the same person or organization is responsible.
5. Specific example: Northstar receives a “purchase breakdown” email
This is an entirely hypothetical teaching scenario. Northstar is an online learning platform. Employee computers support ordinary work but have no permission to read students' private answer data.
Assume investigators, acting under legal authorization, obtain email, endpoint and access records that establish the following case:
The email impersonates a supplier; how the sender learned the contact's details is unknown.

items: Supported interpretation: the source of reconnaissance information remains unknown.
Evidence boundary: do not immediately conclude that the company's address book was stolen.

sourceBody.text: Attachment analysis confirms that it contains malicious content.

items: Supported interpretation: the finished product of weaponization can be analyzed.
Evidence boundary: this does not establish where, when or by whom it was made.

sourceBody.text: Mail records confirm that the attachment reached the employee's inbox.

items: Supported interpretation: Delivery; the targeted malicious attachment behavior can be mapped to T1566.001.
Evidence boundary: arrival does not mean opening or execution.

sourceBody.text: Separate endpoint and sample evidence confirms that a vulnerability in the reader application was exploited to execute malicious code.

items: Supported interpretation: Exploitation; T1203 may apply.
Evidence boundary: not every instance of “opening an attachment” supports this conclusion.

sourceBody.text: Endpoint records confirm that a malicious component was written and installed.

items: Supported interpretation: Installation.
Evidence boundary: writing a file alone still does not establish persistent access after a restart.

sourceBody.text: Correlated analysis confirms that the component exchanged attack commands and responses over HTTPS.

items: Supported interpretation: C2; T1071.001 may apply.
Evidence boundary: an HTTPS connection alone is not proof of C2.

sourceBody.text: The malicious process attempts to read students' private data, but access control denies it.

items: Supported interpretation: an attempt to advance toward the attack objective occurred; this read was blocked.
Evidence boundary: do not claim that the data leaked, or use this result to guarantee that all data is safe.

sourceBody.text: T1203 concerns exploiting client software vulnerabilities to execute code. Apply it only when corresponding evidence exists; do not classify all attachment execution this way. [MITRE: T1203](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/)

T1071.001 describes using web protocols for C2. HTTPS is also widely used for legitimate work, so context such as the process, destination, timing and communication purpose is needed. The protocol name alone does not establish malice. [MITRE: T1071.001](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/)
The real skill this example develops is not “how many labels you added,” but this: every label should sit beside an observation that supports it and a boundary that its conclusion must not exceed.
6. Bring defenses back to “what to block, what to observe and how to verify”
For the hypothetical case above, the following defensive designs could be proposed. Their effectiveness must still be verified in your authorized environment; installed products alone are not proof.
Email filtering and attachment inspection

items: Defensive objective: reduce the likelihood that malicious content reaches users.
Verification focus: was the email actually blocked or quarantined, or did the system merely generate a warning?

sourceBody.text: Software security updates and execution restrictions

items: Defensive objective: reduce opportunities for vulnerability exploitation and improper code execution.
Verification focus: did the update actually take effect? Does safe, authorized validation produce the expected result?

sourceBody.text: Endpoint behavior monitoring

items: Defensive objective: detect abnormal execution, installation and subsequent activity.
Verification focus: are observations tied to the correct device, process and time? Does someone handle the alerts?

sourceBody.text: Necessary outbound connection restrictions

items: Defensive objective: limit unnecessary communications.
Verification focus: did the rule actually block the connection? Do legitimate business functions still work?

sourceBody.text: Least privilege and data-access auditing

items: Defensive objective: limit the data reachable even if an account or process is affected.
Verification focus: use synthetic data and authorized test accounts to confirm that prohibited reads are denied while permitted reads still succeed.

sourceBody.text: Placing defenses at different stages avoids depending on a single checkpoint. AWS's official analysis also uses the attack chain to organize detection and disruption measures at different stages. [AWS: defensive intervention at each stage](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/classic-intrusion-analysis-frameworks-for-aws-environments/stopping-intrusion-methods.html)
Maintain three habits when writing incident conclusions:

1. Write the observation first, then the classification. For example, begin with “mail records show that the attachment was quarantined,” not “the intrusion succeeded” followed by a search for justification.
2. Distinguish attempts, success and impact. Attempting to read, successfully reading, successfully copying and successfully exfiltrating are different events.

3. Preserve unknowns. A missing record might mean that an event did not occur, but it might also reflect missing logging, expired retention or an incomplete query scope. Do not turn “not found” into “guaranteed absent.”

Likewise, an ATT&CK label on a detection rule only claims coverage of a behavior. You still need to test whether the data is collected, the rule works, false positives are acceptable and a real alert can be handled. Classification is not a substitute for validation.
7. Key points and one quick check
Take away four points today:

items: Cyber Kill Chain: examine stages and identify intervention points.
MITRE ATT&CK: examine objectives and behaviors, providing a shared language for analysis.
Do not force all seven stages into an incident or treat ATT&CK as a fixed chronological sequence.
A behavior label does not mean a successful attack; let evidence determine the conclusion.

sourceBody.text: Quick check:

A company receives a targeted email containing a malicious attachment, but its email gateway quarantines it. No evidence has been found that the attachment executed on an employee computer. An analyst writes: “This matches T1566.001, so we have confirmed that the attacker successfully intruded and stole data.”
How would you correct that conclusion? Explain briefly in your own words; you do not need to memorize the identifier.
You can answer this question first. I will assess your understanding after receiving your actual answer.

paragraphs: A more accurate statement is: “We observed a targeted malicious attachment email delivery attempt, which can be mapped to Spearphishing Attachment (T1566.001). The gateway quarantined this email. There is currently insufficient evidence to confirm endpoint execution of the attachment, attacker access or data theft.”

The key point is: T1566.001 is a behavior classification, not proof of a successful intrusion. From a Cyber Kill Chain perspective, we can discuss interception at the delivery stage. We cannot infer that exploitation, installation, C2 or exfiltration all subsequently occurred.

“Execution evidence was not found” also does not prove that the entire environment is free of other intrusions. Check whether logs are complete and whether other copies of the email or other attack paths exist, and limit the conclusion to the scope actually examined.
